description:
A beautifully proportioned two-bedroom garden flat, occupying the raised ground floor of an attractive converted Victorian house, combining impressive period character with elegant and versatile living accommodation and direct access to a wonderful rear garden.

Overview

From the moment you enter, there is a wonderful sense of grandeur and space, with the property retaining a wealth of original Victorian features including high ceilings, and intricate cornicing. The home has been thoughtfully arranged to provide an excellent balance of entertaining space, comfortable bedrooms and useful storage.

The heart of the home is the impressive open-plan kitchen/living room, which occupies much of the front of the property. This is a particularly striking room, benefiting from high ceilings and a large bay window that floods the space with natural light. The bay incorporates a charming built-in seating bench, creating a wonderful spot to sit and enjoy the outlook. The original cornicing adds further character and beautifully complements the scale and elegance of the room. The kitchen area is positioned to one side, allowing the remainder of the room to function as a generous and sociable living and dining space.

Located towards the rear of the property is the principal bedroom, a lovely double room with its own set of French doors opening directly onto the balcony. From here, steps lead down into the beautiful rear garden, creating a rare and particularly appealing connection between the bedroom and outside space. The garden provides a wonderful private area for relaxing, entertaining and enjoying the warmer months, and is a real asset to the property.

The second bedroom benefits from its own en-suite shower room. A charming stained-glass window provides an attractive period feature, adding to the character and individuality of this part of the property. The flat is further complemented by a family bathroom, conveniently positioned off the central hallway and providing a full three-piece suite. There is also excellent practical storage, including useful storage within the hallway false ceiling, helping to keep the principal living spaces uncluttered and providing valuable additional space for household items.

The combination of impressive proportions, original Victorian detailing, high ceilings and a thoughtful layout give the property a real sense of grandeur and elegance, while the balcony and direct access to the rear garden add a contemporary lifestyle appeal that is increasingly sought after.


Location

Situated in the heart of Redland, 7 Chertsey Road offers a fantastic opportunity to acquire a characterful and generously proportioned garden flat within a handsome period conversion. The property would make an excellent home for those seeking space, character and outdoor access in one of Bristol's most desirable residential locations. The property is also within walking proximity to all the conveniences of Whiteladies Road and Clifton Down station.


Material information (provided by owner) 

Remainder of 999 year lease, £65pcm service charge, council tax band C
keyFeatures: Large open-plan kitchen/living room with bay window
Original Victorian features including high ceilings & cornicing
Principal bedroom with French doors onto private balcony
Direct access to a beautiful rear garden
Second bedroom with en-suite & charming stained-glass window
Excellent hallway storage, plus family bathroom
